properties.description: The verdict is pass only when there is nothing at all to report: no confirmed violation, tool error, inconclusive stage, claim or threshold, failed threshold or open finding.
An inconclusive stage, claim or threshold is never a clean pass, whatever inconclusiveBehavior says.
Exit code 0 only for the verdicts pass and pass_with_warnings.
The exit code follows the verdict: policy failure 1, tool error 3, inconclusive 4, success 0, and never 2.
A failed threshold, or a confirmed violation with confirmedViolation: fail, always exits 1.
A stage that failed or errored never exits 0.
With inconclusiveBehavior: fail, an inconclusive item exits 4 unless a policy failure or a tool error takes precedence.
Exit code 1 only for a failed threshold or a confirmed violation with confirmedViolation: fail.
Exit code 3 only for a stage that failed or errored.
Exit code 4 only with inconclusiveBehavior: fail and something inconclusive.
Open findings never make the exit code non-zero without a failed threshold, a failing confirmed violation, a tool error or a failing inconclusive item.

meaningful_with_evidence only with the full evidence: an asserted project call, a relevant kill, mutation results, a linked property, no unexercised boundary, no relevant survivor, no conflicted property, a known link, and a test that runs normally (not expected to fail, type-level only, asserting nothing, skipped or todo).
A test whose link is only possible by name (reachable_by_name) is never meaningful_with_evidence.
A test reachable only by name, with no asserted call and no certainty that it asserts nothing or calls no target, is inconclusive, whether or not it killed mutants.
A test that killed a mutant is never tautological_or_disconnected, unless it asserts nothing or is skipped or todo.
A test that asserts nothing or only constants is tautological_or_disconnected, unless it is expected to fail or type-level only.
A test expected to fail is always inconclusive.
A test that checks only types is always inconclusive.
A skipped or todo test is never meaningful_with_evidence, whatever mutation results are credited to it.
A test that runs, that static analysis found unlinked and that killed a mutant is inconclusive: neither meaningful, weak nor tautological.
Without mutation results a test is never meaningful_with_evidence.
Every evidence record is decided to one of the five test outcomes.
spec_conflict only for a test that asserts a project call and is linked to a conflicted property.
weak_or_incomplete only for a test that asserts a project call, has no conflicted property, and has a relevant surviving mutant (not credited to a skipped or todo test) or an unexercised boundary.
tautological_or_disconnected only from static analysis: the test is not expected to fail or type-level only, and it asserts nothing or no link from it to project code was found.

A test with no asserted call whose link is unknown (an unresolved import, an opaque call, a progress-only check, a caller-supplied suite or name reach) is inconclusive, unless static analysis is certain it asserts nothing or calls no target.
A skipped or todo test gets the same outcome as it would with no kill, no relevant survivor and no mutation results at all.
